memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, "Now you will see what I will do to Pharaoh: Because of my mighty hand he will let them go; because of my mighty hand he will drive them out of his country."" - Exodus 6:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses ended the last chapter with a bitter accusation: you have not rescued your people at all. God's reply begins with one word — now.

Not "how dare you question Me." Not a rebuke. Just: now you will see what I will do.

God was never inactive. He was simply not yet visible. Between Moses' complaint and God's answer, nothing had changed in Egypt — the bricks were still being made without straw. What changed was that God spoke.

Notice how often God says my mighty hand. Twice in one verse. Moses had tried once before, with his own hand, and buried a man in the sand. That failed. This will not, because it is not Moses' strength that is being deployed.

There is a lesson in the timing too. God's "now" came after Moses had run out of every human option. Often God waits until we have stopped trying to arrange the answer ourselves.

Whatever you are waiting on, God's silence is not God's absence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I concluded God is doing nothing, simply because I cannot see it?
2. Am I still trying to accomplish by my own hand what only God's hand can do?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, forgive me for reading Your silence as neglect. Strengthen my faith to wait for Your mighty hand. Amen.
